about.title: Montague Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Montague is a small community, but its roads carry real traffic risk — State Route 3 through 11th Street, Ager Road, Big Springs Road, and N 11th Street see the bulk of reported collisions here. Recent public records show injury crashes do happen in town, often clustering late on Wednesday nights, a pattern that can point to fatigue, low visibility, or impaired driving. Whatever the cause, a crash on a rural highway or a quiet residential street can leave you dealing with pain, medical bills, and a vehicle that's no longer drivable. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect Montague residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options. There's no fee upfront, and the attorneys in our network only get paid if you recover compensation. Reaching out early, before evidence disappears or memories fade, tends to matter most in a town this size.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Other Insurer Calls

items.title: The Clock on Your Claim Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a lawsuit, but that window can shrink to just six months if a government entity, like a county road authority, was involved. Waiting to sort this out can quietly cost you your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Be Used Against You
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning an insurer may try to pin partial blame on you to reduce what they pay. An independent attorney can push back on that narrative before it's baked into the record.

items.title: Recorded Statements Rarely Help You
items.desc: California law places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but insurers often try to minimize claims early through recorded statements. Speaking with an attorney first helps make sure your words aren't used to undercut your own case.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash near 11th Street in Montague — what should I do first?
items.answer: Get medical attention and, if possible, document the scene, vehicle damage, and any visible injuries. Avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer until you've spoken with an independent attorney, since early statements can be used to shift blame. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney at no cost to help sort out next steps.

items.question: What if the crash happened on a county or state road, like Route 3?
items.answer: Claims involving government-maintained roads can carry a much shorter filing deadline, sometimes as little as six months instead of the usual two years. Because Montague's higher-traffic corridors include state and county roads, it's worth having an attorney check the specifics of your crash location quickly.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no cost or obligation just to have a conversation about what happened.
